correspondence.component_scope: Northern selected opening and southern Pocitos-side passage
correspondence.finding: The northern original places the selected opening beside the southwestern side of the saline area printed Pocitos o Quirón. The selection proceeds south and turns west below the Sierra de Calalaste setting. No original channel line establishes this full opening-to-westward connection. It does not follow the separately mapped Vega Navarro drainage farther west or the Tolar Chico–Tolillar salars farther east.

correspondence.component_scope: Local feeder to northern Vega Juncalito
correspondence.finding: Southwest of the unresolved northern turn, an unnamed blue watercourse is drawn toward the wetland and locality labeled Vega Juncalito/Juncalito at the northern end of Salar de Antofalla. The selected upper approach occupies this local feeder corridor. This visible local continuation does not supply the missing connection from the far northern opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern and middle eastern Salar de Antofalla margin
correspondence.finding: The original labels the north–south saline depression Salar de Antofalla. The selection follows its eastern margin south from the northern Juncalito surroundings, opposite the Sierra de Aguas Calientes and western side of the Calalaste range. The cartography shows salt-flat terrain, local entering drainages and nearby wetland settings, but no continuous selected longitudinal river or established surface-water passage along all of this margin.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern continuation beside Agua Negra and the Calalaste terrain
correspondence.finding: The selected route continues southwest over mapped marginal terrain east and southeast of the historical Salar de Antofalla outline. It passes the Agua Negra surroundings west of Alto Calalaste and crosses several separate local drainage traces. The map does not show a corresponding connected longitudinal channel. The directly labeled R. Calalaste lies farther east; the directly labeled R. Antofalla approaches the salar from the west by Antofalla village and is not the chosen long northern branch.

correspondence.component_scope: Final westward bend near the southern Vega Juncalito surroundings
correspondence.finding: The actual selected ending bends west and then northwest in the southeastern Antofalla marginal setting, south of the second, southern Vega Juncalito label and west of Vega Achi. The historical original exposes the terrain and small local water features but does not establish the complete selected final connection or its receiving channel. Earlier lawful article prose separately describes Antofalla as internally drained and the Las Quínoas western wetland as feeding short local channels into the salt flat. Those local observations do not identify this selected endpoint or connect it to the northern route.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen headward opening and northward arch
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening, the northeastward opening segment, the succession of short parts and the complete northern turn are all within the regional original’s continuous inland-ice area. The full opening is south of the sheet’s northern neatline. The mapped ice contours are not a named river or proof of a watercourse following the selected arch.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastward and eastward inland-ice sequence
correspondence.finding: All selected southeastward and eastward parts and their intermediate joins remain within contiguous mapped inland ice. The source exposes the entire succession, including its eastward steps and the bend toward the lower margin. No named natural-river reach or surface/subglacial through-link is established by that ice-and-contour correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward turn and lower ice with scattered rock
correspondence.finding: The southward turn and subsequent eastward small bends pass from broad inland ice into ice containing scattered exposed-rock or nunatak outlines. The entire succession and its joins are visible in the same regional original. These rock patches and ice contours do not establish a chain of connected river reaches, lakes, reservoirs or managed channels.

correspondence.component_scope: Final eastward approach and southeastward bend
correspondence.finding: The final eastward approach and southeastward bend continue through the mapped ice-and-scattered-rock belt inland of Napasorsuup Kangerlua / Napasorsuaq Fjord. The selected approach is covered continuously and is distinguished from the neighboring mapped coastal water and rock peninsulas. No glacier name is assigned and no hydraulic connection is inferred from geographic proximity.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual final selected part and terminal setting
correspondence.finding: The entire last selected part and actual rendered endpoint are in the generalized ice/exposed-rock margin at the inland side of the mapped Napasorsuup Kangerlua / Napasorsuaq Fjord head. The original distinguishes surrounding ice, exposed rock and the white coastal-water inlet. The model’s sea-terminal metadata is not independent evidence of an ordinary river mouth. The source’s historical epoch and thematic scale do not establish an exact current ice front or current land/ice/water assignment at the endpoint.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual northeastern opening and Nabón descent
correspondence.finding: Thesis map10 depicts and labels Río León at the actual northeastern chosen opening and follows its west-then-southwest course through the Nabón sector. The selected main corridor continues past the local feeder joins; nearby Charcay and other tributary labels are not transferred to it. Map3 supplies overlapping regional context.

correspondence.component_scope: León through the Oña-side valley
correspondence.finding: Maps3 and4 show the continuous southwestward León corridor along the Oña-side valley toward La Unión, distinguish the eastern Oña tributaries and the southern Naranjo approach, and expose the selected westward bend.

correspondence.component_scope: La Unión bend and northward León continuation
correspondence.finding: Map3 follows the selected northward León reach from the La Unión setting to its receiving junction below the separate Rircay approach. Map1 corroborates the León subbasin arrangement. The thesis geographic prose identifies the León–Rircay union as the start of Jubones proper.

correspondence.component_scope: Jubones receiving junction and westward middle valley
correspondence.finding: Maps1 and3 expose the common westward receiving corridor and ordinary lateral joins. Map1 distinguishes the Uchucay, Minas and Ganacay side basins; the prose supports Jubones below the León–Rircay union. The boundary between river names is not assigned to an exact model vertex.

correspondence.component_scope: Minas San Francisco reservoir and dam transition
correspondence.finding: The December2020 INSITU article Figure1 directly depicts the reservoir, distinct San Francisco inflow, dam/stilling-basin setting and westward Río Jubones below it. This supplies bounded structural geography for the selected middle-valley crossing alongside the historical basin map. No current level, release, operating status or uninterrupted natural-river passage is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Jubones valley before the coastal divergence
correspondence.finding: CELEC/CESEL-CTOTAL sheet MT A-4 directly labels Río Jubones and follows the lower valley westward through the Pasaje-side corridor, with lateral drainage distinguishable from the trunk. The MCRJ basin map supplies overlapping regional continuation. Local model/cartographic offsets do not change this bounded valley correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected final coastal-plain passage and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: The selected line takes a more southerly western route and reaches a different near-coastal ending from the downstream Jubones course drawn in MT A-4. The broad MCRJ basin map likewise shows a more northerly outlet. Neither source establishes the selected final connection; a pale nearby channel, basin membership and the model sea classification are insufficient. No unnamed reach is assigned a guessed channel name.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen eastern opening and unnamed lakeward feeder
correspondence.finding: The CEHQ original depicts the selected small eastern watercourse from its chosen opening westward through the successive bends to the southern approach of Lac du Vieux Comptoir. The route is distinct from the neighboring longer southern watercourse. The reserve annex supplies matching regional feeder and lake context, but the CEHQ watercourse linework is the decisive detailed correspondence. Neither original inspected establishes a separate feeder name or an ultimate natural source.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake entry, Lac du Vieux Comptoir passage and southwestern outlet
correspondence.finding: The selected approach bends north into the mapped lake, crosses its main connected water body and leaves by the southwestward outlet before the westward river turn. CEHQ labels the lake Lac du Vieux-Comptoir; the reserve annex labels Lac du Vieux Comptoir and shows its river connections. The selected course does not follow the separate northern Lac McNab approach or extend to the eastern Opinaca impoundment. No precise inlet/outlet bank or lake-versus-river name-boundary vertex is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward receiving river and intermediate joins
correspondence.finding: West of the lake outlet, the selected course follows the mapped westward bends and intervening tributary joins before turning southwest toward the coast. The reserve annex places Rivière du Vieux Comptoir along this connected receiving-river corridor and distinguishes Rivière du Peuplier to the north. CEHQ depicts the same connected course and separates the Tilorier, Renoyer and Conn drainage corridors farther south. These surrounding names are orientation checks, not alternative names for the selected river.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwest lower course, coastal branching and James Bay terminal
correspondence.finding: The selected lower course continues southwest from the main westward bend, follows the mapped northern course through the low coastal branching setting and reaches James Bay. CEHQ shows the selected through-connection to the coast as well as the adjoining southern branch; the reserve annex confirms the named lower river and its bay outlet. The terminal is treated as a mapped river-to-bay connection, without claiming a surveyed mouth point, exact tidal bank, individual island passage or present shoreline.
